meeting_header:
Date: 2026-04-08
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Rodriguez (Celestia Head of Data), Tom Nguyen (Celestia Platform), Priya Kapoor (Celestia CISO)
summary: Redwood demo focused on Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown for Celestia Health's inference workloads. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) for PHI-adjacent prompts, wants token-level cost visibility, route-based allocation, and alerts tied to quality regressions. Agreed next steps: sample dataset + traffic profile, 24h benchmark, pilot pricing + SOW, share security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Owen, our solutions engineer. How's it going?
[00:12] Lina: Hi Maya, hi Owen. Thanks for doing this. We wanted a focused walkthrough of the Console — specifically the usage analytics and cost stuff. We're trying to understand per-route attribution.
[00:25] Owen: Great, that's exactly what we'll cover. Quick agenda: we'll show the high-level dashboard, then drill into per-route views, token-level cost, and then how alerts and evals tie into the console.
[00:35] Tom: Quick context — we run multiple product routes: triage-bot, clinician-assistant, notes-summarizer. Triage has the most volume, clinician-assistant needs low latency, notes-summarizer is heavy tokens.
[00:47] Owen: Perfect, that maps well to the per-route dashboards. One thing to note up front: our Console can attribute cost by route, by model version, and by tag (you can tag requests with customer_id, team, or billing code).
[00:58] Priya: Also want to confirm — we're healthcare, so SOC 2 controls, KMS for key management, and data residency are musts. How does the Console surface audit logs?
[01:10] Maya: We'll show the audit log view later. For KMS and residency — we have Private deployments and Dedicated options; we'll link the SOC 2 and network diagrams after the call.
[01:20] Owen: Alright, jumping into screen share — top-left is the Usage Overview; you can see total tokens in, tokens out, avg latency, and cost burn over time.
[01:32] [01:32] Owen: Here we've got token trend lines, and if you click into a time window it'll show the top routes by spend.
[01:45] Lina: Can you filter by model variant? We run both 13B quantized and a 34B float for critical paths.
[01:53] Owen: Yep — model variant filter is here. You can also compare across variants to see cost vs latency tradeoffs. Note: sometimes the auto-transcribe says 'thirty four B' as 'thirty for B' in older logs — ignore that, that's transcription noise.
[02:10] Owen: Quick demo of a per-route dashboard — selecting 'clinician-assistant'. You can see request rate, median/95th latency, cost per 1k tokens, and token distribution by request type.
[02:25] Tom: Is cost per 1k tokens showing both infra and model compute? We need breakdowns for our chargeback.
[02:33] Owen: Yes, we show model compute cost, infra overhead, and any reserved capacity amortization. You can export a CSV with per-route breakdowns for the last 30/90/365 days.
[02:45] Owen: One useful view is the token-level heatmap — it shows avg tokens per request over time so you can spot spikes from long conversations or hallucination loops.
[02:56] Lina: Nice. Can we set alerts on token spikes or cost per route?
[03:03] Owen: Absolutely — alerting supports thresholds on tokens/hour, cost/day, latency SLO breaches, and also custom eval-based alerts (so if your quality eval drops against a prompt suite we can fire an alert).
[03:16] Priya: About the eval alerts — are the evals run in-redwood or do we integrate our own evaluation system?
[03:24] Owen: Both — you can upload your evals or use our evals runner. The Console ties eval results back to route and model, and you can configure regression windows and automatic rollback policies for rollouts.
[03:37] [03:37] Owen: Showing cost attribution by tag now — you can pass metadata with each request (e.g., team:care, team:ops) and the Console will split spend accordingly.
[03:50] Tom: That's important. Our finance team wants allocation by product-line and by environment (prod vs staging).
[03:57] Owen: You can set default tags at route-level and override per-request. Also we have a cost model editor — you can set weights for reserved capacity amortization vs on-demand.
[04:10] Lina: About accuracy of attribution — if requests hit the KV cache, are those tokens excluded from downstream token costs?
[04:18] Owen: Good call, we show cache hit rates. When a request is served from prefix or KV cache the Console marks those tokens as cache-saved and adjusts the token accounting. There's a K-V cash spelled K V cash stuff occasionally in transcripts, but functionally it's the KV cache.
[04:33] Maya: Quick digression on hosted vs dedicated — you mentioned reserved capacity amortization — if you go Dedicated we can show effective per-token cost after reserved commit, which often drops the per-token compute.
[04:46] Tom: We're leaning private for PHI concerns but want to compare costs. Does the Console let us model a hypothetical Dedicated commit?
[04:55] Owen: Yes, the cost simulator lets you input commit size and region and it will project per-token costs and show break-even points vs hosted.
[05:05] Lina: Can the simulator incorporate our real traffic profile?
[05:09] Owen: You can upload a CSV of your traffic profile and it will run the projection against that. That's what we'll do in the benchmark step.
[05:18] [05:18] Owen: Moving to per-route examples — here's notes-summarizer: high token counts, lower QPS. The Console highlights the top prompts contributing to token spend so you can optimize prompt design or implement truncation.
[05:32] Tom: Is prompt-level tracing a privacy concern? We need options to redact stored prompts or only send hashes to Redwood.
[05:40] Maya: On that point — we support configurable retention and PII redaction. For Private deployments you can configure zero retention on our side and keep traces in your VPC. We'll share the security doc.
[05:52] Priya: KMS integration — are keys customer-managed? Because compliance wants customer key control.
[05:58] Owen: For Private and Dedicated, yes — KMS/HSM integration with customer-managed keys is supported. In Hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS in many cases.
[06:10] [06:10] Owen: Back to dashboards — the per-route timeline view shows model version rollouts. You can hover to see when a canary was promoted and the delta in latency and cost.
[06:22] Lina: Talk me through rollbacks — can we auto-roll back on quality regression?
[06:26] Owen: Yep, you can set automatic rollback policies tied to eval thresholds or increased latency. You can also set staged canaries (10%, 30%, 100%).
[06:35] Lina: Who executes the rollback? Our ops or Redwood?
[06:39] Owen: Typically it's automated by the Console per policy, but you can require manual approval. For Private installs you can run the control plane locally so that rollouts are under your control.
[06:53] [06:53] Tom: About the benchmarking — can we run synthetic load from your dedicated infra in our target region?
[06:59] Owen: We offer a benchmarking harness. For Dedicated/Private we can run it in-region. For hosted we simulate similar traffic shapes. We'll need your sample prompt set and expected QPS.
[07:10] Maya: If we see cost anomalies we also have per-token audit trails and request payloads (if retained) so you can debug weird loops or large token usage.
[07:21] Priya: Will those payloads contain PHI? We prefer redaction, or storing only the hash.
[07:27] Owen: You can configure redaction rules and choose to store only metadata+hash. We'll add that to the security pack doc.
[07:35] [07:35] Owen: Quick question for Lina — what's an acceptable latency for clinician-assistant?
[07:39] Lina: 200ms median, 400ms p95 ideally. Anything above 800ms is too slow for the clinicians.
[07:47] Owen: Good, we'll aim to demonstrate 200/400 in the benchmark. If we need lower latency we recommend a smaller quantized model or dedicated GPUs with lower sequence-length pipeline.
[07:58] Tom: On quantization — do you show quality regressions when we swap from 34B float to 13B int8?
[08:05] Owen: The Console's baseline comparison will show eval metrics side-by-side for candidate model variants so you can see regressions by test prompt.
[08:14] [08:14] Owen: Now showing Cost Explorer — you can group by route, by tag, by model, and apply custom date ranges. Exports include per-request token counts and cost.
[08:27] Lina: How granular is the export? We need to feed it into our internal chargeback system weekly.
[08:32] Owen: You can export daily or hourly aggregates, and a per-request log for a rolling 30-day window (retention configurable). For longer retention we can push to your S3 in Private/Dedicated.
[08:46] Priya: Is the per-request log PII masked by default?
[08:50] Owen: Defaults are conservative (redacted), but you can opt-in to store full payloads in a secured bucket with KMS.
[08:58] Maya: Quick note on how we calculate effective per-token cost: we factor model execution cost, GPU amortization (if reserved), infra overhead, and margin. You can toggle which components to include in the Console view.
[09:12] Tom: Can we set internal rates? Finance wants to charge teams at a slightly higher rate to cover platform ops.
[09:18] Owen: Yes, there's a markup field in the cost model. You can publish internal per-route rates and the console will compute internal chargebacks.
[09:28] [09:28] Owen: Now I'll demo the alert-to-action flow — an eval alert triggered on a regression for notes-summarizer. The Console shows failing prompts, affected route, and suggested rollback.
[09:41] Lina: Does it integrate with PagerDuty / Slack?
[09:44] Owen: Yep — webhooks, PagerDuty, Slack, and email. You can set escalation policies per alert.
[09:54] Priya: For compliance we need audit trails of who acknowledged an alert.
[09:58] Owen: Audit logs capture user actions (who approved rollback, who changed policies). Those logs are exportable and time-stamped.
[10:10] [10:10] Tom: A practical question — what's the approximate cost delta between hosted and a 3-month reserved commit for our profile?
[10:18] Owen: It depends on commit size and region; the simulator shows typical drops of 20-45% for steady high-volume routes. We'll run your profile to get precise numbers.
[10:27] Lina: We'll share last quarter's traffic CSV after the call.
[10:31] Owen: Great. Next I want to show the per-route drilldown where you can click a spike and see the request traces — it surfaces prompt, tokens in/out, model variant, and cache hit.
[10:44] [10:44] Owen: There's also a feature we call "cost anomaly detection" that looks for unusual per-request cost increases and flags suspect prompts or loops.
[10:55] Tom: Could that help find runaway loops in our orchestrator?
[10:57] Owen: Exactly. It detects sudden increases in tokens-per-request and can auto-notify.
[11:05] Lina: About tagging and chargebacks — can the Console split cost across multiple tags on a single request? For instance, a request belonging to two teams.
[11:15] Owen: We support proportional split by configured weights. You can set tag weight defaults and override per-request.
[11:24] [11:24] Maya: Let's shift to security questions from Priya.
[11:27] Priya: We need monthly penetration testing, SOC 2 Type II, SIEM integration. Also, may need an on-prem option for air-gapped research.
[11:38] Owen: We have SOC 2 Type II, pen-test reports on request, and SIEM integration via syslog or pushing to your S3. For air-gapped on-prem we have an appliance-based package.
[11:49] Priya: And SSO / RBAC?
[11:51] Maya: SSO via SAML and OIDC, and role-based access controls with fine-grained permissions for viewing costs vs releasing rollouts.
[11:59] Tom: Any limits to RBAC for per-route visibility? We want only finance to see cost metrics for certain teams.
[12:06] Owen: RBAC supports scoped dashboards so you can hide or show cost columns based on role.
[12:14] [12:14] Owen: Back to the cost breakdown UI — note the "what-if" slider for reserved commit sizing; I'll show it set to 6 months.
[12:26] Lina: Can the Console project break-even per route if we migrate certain routes to smaller models?
[12:33] Owen: Yes, you can create scenarios: change model type, change quantization, change commit size, and it'll re-run the projection against your uploaded traffic.
[12:44] Tom: For the pilot, can we do a split-run of triage-bot 50/50 between hosted and a Dedicated pool?
[12:51] Owen: You can route percentage traffic by policy. We'll show how to configure that in the routing section.
[13:00] [13:00] Owen: Now exposing the route history view — shows historical rollouts, model versions, and cost spikes. Here's a past case where a bad prompt increased tokens 10x and triggered an alert.
[13:15] Lina: Is there a way to auto-suggest prompt edits or truncation points?
[13:19] Owen: We have recommendations in Optimize — it will suggest truncation thresholds, caching prefixes, and batching configs for cost savings based on the prompt distribution.
[13:31] Maya: That ties into Redwood Optimize — we'll include that in the pilot proposal.
[13:36] Priya: Any compliance constraints for storing prompt-level evals? We might want to keep only aggregated metrics.
[13:44] Owen: Defaults can be aggregated only; storing detailed traces is opt-in with additional controls.
[13:52] [13:52] Tom: Regarding monitoring, can we stream metrics to our Prometheus/Grafana stack?
[13:58] Owen: Yes — metrics can be pushed to your metrics endpoint or exported via Prom remote write. Dashboards are pre-built.
[14:08] Lina: Great. One more thing — our product team wants per-feature cost allocation for feature flags.
[14:15] Owen: Tag your requests with feature_flag=... and the console will show per-flag spend.
[14:22] [14:22] Owen: We're nearing the last part — sharing the security pack, SOW template, and pilot pricing.
[14:29] Maya: Recap of what we'll send: pilot pricing + SOW, SOC 2 + pen test, KMS integration guide, sample benchmark plan.
[14:38] Lina: And you'll do the 24h benchmark once we share traffic and prompts?
[14:42] Owen: Correct — we'll run it and share the latency/cost spreadsheet and recommended commit size.
[14:49] Priya: Locking down access during the pilot — can we restrict RBAC to a small set of users?
[14:54] Maya: Yes, we'll provision a minimal admin set and add others as needed.
[15:01] [15:01] Tom: Timeline question — how fast can we stand up a Private deployment?
[15:06] Owen: For Private on-prem appliance it's 6-8 weeks; for VPC-hosted Private it can be 2-4 weeks depending on network provisioning and certs. That said, pilots often start on Hosted with data redaction while provisioning Private.
[15:22] Lina: That might be the path for us.
[15:26] Owen: Any final questions on the Console functionality?
[15:30] Lina: No, looks good. We'll share traffic CSV.
[15:33] Priya: Please send the security docs.
[15:36] Maya: We'll send docs and pricing today/tomorrow. Owen will run the benchmark once we get the dataset.
[15:43] [15:43] Owen: Quick aside — we sometimes see transcription glitches in Fireflies where product names show up weirdly (e.g., "re-dwood" instead of Redwood) — just flag if anything looks off.
[15:55] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the next steps.
[16:00] [16:00] End of recording

Action items captured in the call: Maya to send SOW/pilot pricing; Tom to share traffic & prompt set; Owen to run benchmark and share cost/latency spreadsheet; Priya to confirm KMS/residency requirements.

Notes on transcription: Medium quality — occasional mis-words (K-V cash / re-dwood), some punctuation missing.
